title: Total royal revenue and mint revenue (seigniorage), France 1286–1480 and England 1323–1547
source: Arthur J. Rolnick, François R. Velde and Warren E. Weber, 'The Debasement Puzzle: An Essay on Medieval Monetary History', Journal of Economic History 56(4): 789–808 (1996); reprinted in Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis Quarterly Review 21(4): 8–20 (Fall 1997), Tables 2 and 3
series: Tables 2 and 3 'Total Government Revenues and Seigniorage in Medieval France and England': Table 2 France, 1286–1480 (current livres tournois, unless specified otherwise), Table 3 England, 1323–1547 (current pounds sterling); columns Period, Annual Revenues (Thou.) Total and Mint, Mint as % of Total. Here: country, period, marks (footnote signs), total_thousand, mint_thousand, mint_pct (blank where the table prints a dash)
license: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis Quarterly Review, freely available on the Bank's research database; a 26-row table transcribed for teaching and comment, with attribution.
notes: Transcribed from the text layer of the reprint (PDF SHA-256 7bf063565911d476c0cad71db091c1eee5ec0b02f362283fa882934388534ee5, page 13) and compared with the printed page, because the text layer renders the dagger as 't' and drops a footnote sign. Footnotes, Table 2 (France): * 'Debasement occurred during this or the preceding year.' † 'Period is the first half of the year; amounts are at an annual rate.' § 'Period is the second half of the year; amounts are at an annual rate.' ** (on 97.7, 1354–60) 'Amount is in 1330 currency; in 1361 currency, it is 162.5 thousand.' Footnotes, Table 3 (England): * 'Debasement occurred during this period.' † 'The sales of monasteries accounted for £60,000 in the years 1535–39, £144,000 in the years 1540–44, and £135,000 in the years 1545–47.' § 'Taxes, parliamentary or otherwise, amounted to £0.92 million in the years 1540–47, or £115,000 annually.' ** 'Mint revenues were £1.2 million in the years 1544–51, or £150,000 annually.' The England total for 1463–66 is printed in parentheses, (30). The sources of the table are French and English fiscal histories listed under it (Saulcy, Vuitry, Fawtier, Lot and Fawtier, Rey, Pocquet de Haut-Jussé; Steel, Williams, Dietz, Mayhew, Challis); the authors call the data 'very fragmentary'. Check (checks/check_ch11.py): mint/total × 100 rounds to the printed percentage in every row that has both.
